I updated our sidebar rules as follows:

  • Licensed - Never post links to a manga that is licensed unless they are official links (ie Crunchyroll). Including links to buy the material is highly encouraged.

  • Unlicensed - You may post links to this series (bato.to or original scalnator websites are preferred), links to the original Japanese release are highly encouraged as well. If the series becomes licensed, the mods will send original thread posters 3 warnings to change links before deleting posts.

  • If you post multiple discussions for the same series, it is highly recommended that you post an Archive in /v/metamanga that is linked from every post, to assist in organization for readers.

This change came about after a few users voiced some very real concerns about how additional rules outlined here would stifle contributions to the sub. I'd like to thank those users for pointing things out; us mods will always at least consider constructive feedback that we are given.
If this community does grow, will you be able to keep track of all posts linking to unlicensed manga, and react accordingly when one is licenced?
We will try our best to keep up! We just added someone to the mod team and will add more people if needed in the future.

I see. Good luck in that case.

May I ask how you decide whom to accept as a mod? What are the criteria?

We look at quality of participation in whichever sub we're looking at (/v/anime or /v/manga, since 2 mods overlap and they're very similar) and if someone's in the IRC that gives them a leg up as well because we feel we know the person more. It's also dependent on need, we won't ask someone unless we feel we need more because we don't want "too many cooks in the kitchen" so to speak.

This sub (like everything else, in my opinion) is still a work in progress, you'll see another change to the rules later today once we finish ironing some things out. (I think it's bad to think of things as 'finished', because I feel it connotes 'no more change' or 'no need for change'.)

Thanks for clearing it up. It feels like you are open to the users as a mod, and I hope it stays so. I'm liking this place, after all.

Cheers

Yes, if people are active, passionate and seem like they would be a big asset to the team I see no reason why we would not invite them when needed :)

Even if people aren't mods, if they have something to say about the sub we will at least read and consider their opinion (see: this rule change).

I personally think people should only mod as much as they can commit to. I know @moe mods a few bigger subs, but he does try to dedicate as much time as he can to /v/anime and /v/manga in regards to posting regularly and giving useful input to management decisions. Basically, as long as a person can commit to their mod duties regularly, I have no problems.
